elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause opens: "On expiry or termination of this Agreement or an Order Form for any reason, Vendor shall ..."

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: (a) "at Customer's request, provide transition assistance for up to six months".

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: (b) "within thirty days, return all Customer Data", anchored to the opening "On expiry or termination ... for any reason".

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: (c) "after that return, delete Customer Data from its systems and certify the deletion to Customer in writing".

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Same opening trigger: "On expiry or termination of this Agreement or an Order Form for any reason".

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: Up to six months of transition assistance exceeds the 90-day fallback floor.

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: (b) requires return of all Customer Data in a machine-readable format within thirty days, satisfying the export duty.

reasons: All six preferred elements are present in one concise inserted paragraph; the preferred level is complete, and the fallback level is also satisfied.

The insertion adds no extras beyond the checklist: no survival tail, no at-own-expense language, no additional procedures or damages categories; the 'at Customer's request' qualifier and 'for any reason' trigger track the checklist scope.

Existing §§ 10.1, 10.2 and 16.5 are retained verbatim with no deletions or paraphrase; the new clause supplies the transition obligation that § 10.1 previously only assumed ('any agreed transition period') without contradicting it.

No undefined terms or dangling cross-references are introduced; 'Customer Data', 'Order Form', 'Vendor' and 'Customer' are all defined, and § 16.5's deferral of Customer Data to Sections 11 and 15 is unaffected because the new clause sits in the termination section and adds rather than conflicts.
Note only (not a defect): the clause is placed after § 10.2 without a section number in the rendered text; the drafter should confirm it is numbered § 10.3 on execution.
